CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFHEADER

CFHEADER writes a custom line into the HTTP response header: cache control, expiry dates, a Content-Disposition for downloads, or any header of your own. With STATUSCODE it changes the status line instead.

Category

Output and page processing

Syntax

<CFHEADER NAME="header_name"
    VALUE="header_value">

<CFHEADER STATUSCODE="status_code"
    STATUSTEXT="status_text">

Attributes

NAME
Required if STATUSCODE is not given. Name of the header, for example "Expires" or "Cache-Control".
VALUE
Optional. Value of the header.
STATUSCODE
Required if NAME is not given. HTTP status code, for example 404 or 503.
STATUSTEXT
Optional. Text that follows the status code in the status line, for example "Not Found".

Usage

Headers are collected while the page runs and sent when it finishes, so CFHEADER can appear anywhere in the page. Setting the same header twice keeps the last value. A Content-Type header is the same as CFCONTENT TYPE.

HTTP dates must be in GMT and in the RFC 1123 format; GetHTTPTimeString makes one for you. To see the headers your page sends, use View, Page Info in Netscape Navigator. Cookies have their own tag, CFCOOKIE.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Tell browsers and proxies not to keep a copy of this page --->
<CFSET Stamp = GetHTTPTimeString(Now())>
<CFHEADER NAME="Expires" VALUE="#Stamp#">
<CFHEADER NAME="Pragma" VALUE="no-cache">
<CFHEADER NAME="Cache-Control" VALUE="no-cache, must-revalidate">
<CFHEADER NAME="X-Snippet" VALUE="CFHEADER example">

<P>This response was sent with these extra headers:</P>
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR BGCOLOR="##CCCCFF"><TH>Header</TH><TH>Value</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>Expires</TD><TD>#Stamp#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Pragma</TD><TD>no-cache</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>Cache-Control</TD><TD>no-cache, must-revalidate</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>X-Snippet</TD><TD>CFHEADER example</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>
